categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK (5/5; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's ImageSharp NuGet advisories, not the model's). / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the Blog page, but renders only 'No blocks to display.' (Model.Blocks count 0, see the DEBUG comment in pages/index.html). There is no post listing and no links to the posts (1/10). Both posts render without errors: featured image, title, author, date and a rich-text bodyText property. Their block grids are empty, so no block renders on a post (4/10). The provided Unsplash photos were imported into a media folder, and the featured images go through GetCropUrl and load. The hero's background image never shows because the hero block doesn't render (4/5). Domain '/' is on the Blog page and everything is published (5/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders and kinds are right: heroBlock and blogPostListBlock are elements in Blocks, blogFrontPage and blogPost are in Pages, siteRoot is in Repositories (8/8). Block grid: one shared 'Block Grid' data type is on both page types, but the block set is only hero plus post list. There is no rich text or image block, so the post body is a plain RTE property and both post grids are empty (2/7). Structure is clean: only siteRoot at root, siteRoot → blogFrontPage → blogPost, templates assigned, camelCase aliases, data type in /Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid (5/5). Hygiene: no compositions, and date, excerpt, author and featured image are real properties. The front page carries unused excerpt and featuredImage properties. The front page's block value was hand-built with placeholder keys and an empty 'expose' list, so nothing is exposed (4/5).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: The pages call Html.PartialAsync("blockgrid/default", Model.Blocks) instead of Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync. That reuses the scaffold partials, which are unchanged, and there is no custom block loop: the check's FAIL is the post loop inside the list block (4/7). The adapters sit at the right path with the exact aliases, but they take untyped BlockGridItem and cast it, contain all the markup, map to no plain model and never call Component.InvokeAsync. blogPostListBlock also queries content by walking ContentAtRoot (1/6). There are no ViewComponents, no plain view models in Models/<Folder>/ and no Views/Shared/Components (0/7). Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations, and GetCropUrl is used. But Tailwind comes from the CDN script rather than the wwwroot/dist/site.css pipeline, both templates set Layout = null with duplicated HTML shells, and a DEBUG comment is left in blogFrontPage.cshtml (3/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two posts genuinely about why MCP is useful ('Why MCP is a Game-Changer…', 'How MCP Connects AI to the Real World'). They are accurate and reasonably substantive, at about 3–4 paragraphs plus a bullet list each. But each post is a single rich-text property with one featured image, not spread over blocks (3/6). The front page screenshot is an empty page reading 'No blocks to display.' with a footer. The post page is clean and readable, with a rounded header image, meta row and body text. The body's h2/ul styling is lost because the 'prose' class has no typography plugin, so headings show as plain text (1/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema and content were built only through the Umbraco MCP server (42 calls, 22 writes). The run used no migrations, DB, Management API or browser, and followed the order modeling → content → Razor → restart. The stayedInFolder and intendedChannel checks pass, with no memory or bench-folder access (3/3). There is no final report: the benchmark guard stopped the run at its 8M-token budget while the model was debugging the empty front page. So the broken front page was never disclosed (0/2).

summary: Through MCP, the model built a correctly filed schema (hero and post-list blocks, front page and post types under siteRoot, '/' domain) and two posts about MCP with Unsplash featured images that render cleanly. But the front page's block grid renders nothing, so the site has no post listing. The posts use a rich-text property instead of blocks, there are no ViewComponents, and the run was cut off by the token budget before any final report.
strengths: Document types filed in the right folders with the right kinds; clean siteRoot → blogFrontPage → blogPost structure with templates and a '/' domain
All schema and content built through the Umbraco MCP server, in the required order, without leaving the project folder
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served via GetCropUrl
Post pages render cleanly with featured image, author, date and accurate MCP content

issues.text: Front page (/) renders only 'No blocks to display.': Model.Blocks is empty at render time (the hand-built block value has placeholder keys and an empty 'expose' list). So there is no post listing and no links to the posts (Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml, pages/index.html).

Posts don't use the block grid: their 'blocks' value is empty and the body is a single rich-text 'bodyText' property. The block set has no rich text or image block (snapshot.json, Views/blogPost.cshtml).
No ViewComponents or plain view models: both adapters (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/heroBlock.cshtml, blogPostListBlock.cshtml) hold all the markup and never call Component.InvokeAsync.
No final report: the benchmark guard stopped the run at the 8M-token budget mid-debugging, so the broken front page went undisclosed.
Pages render blocks via Html.PartialAsync("blockgrid/default", Model.Blocks) instead of Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync.
Tailwind loaded from cdn.tailwindcss.com instead of the wwwroot/dist/site.css pipeline. Both templates use Layout = null with duplicated HTML shells. A DEBUG comment is left in blogFrontPage.cshtml.
blogPostListBlock.cshtml finds posts by walking Umbraco.ContentAtRoot() children inside a view.
